maya: Quick ping to sec — PR ready for a fast review if someone has bandwidth. https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2847 :point_up:

maya: This changes the auth flow for Private deployments and adds an optional KMS-backed envelope encryption path for on-prem. Main concerns: secrets at rest + rotation, config surface for customers, and ensuring no key material is logged. Hoping to merge today if green.

deploy-bot: CI: all checks passed (build ✅, unit tests ✅, lint ✅) — 1792104380

sam: @maya thanks — can you TL;DR the key management model? envelope vs direct, where DEKs live, rotation plan, and whether customers can bring their own KMS key? :eyes:

maya: Sure — short:+
- Envelope encryption: we generate a DEK per-deployment, encrypt it with the customer/master key from KMS (optional).
- Encrypted DEK is stored in the deployment metadata table in Postgres (ciphertext only).
- On startup the runtime calls KMS to unwrap DEK into memory, never writes plaintext to disk.
- Rotation: we rewrap DEKs when a new master key is provided; there's a migration job that rewraps batchwise to avoid downtime.
- BYOK: supported via config.kms.key_arn (customer-managed).

maya: Example config snippet:
```yaml
encryption:
  provider: aws_kms
  key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
  require_audit_log: true
```

alice: Quick ask — is there an explicit assertion that we never log plaintext DEKs? we should add a runtime check + unit that fails if any path writes DEK to disk or logs it. Also add e2e for rotate-to-new-key.

jon: Does this touch hosted API routing or only Private/Dedicated? want to ensure we don't accidentally call customer KMS from hosted control plane.

maya: Only Private/Dedicated. Hosted uses our managed key and a different code path (no BYOK). PR has a guard that prevents BYOK config in hosted namespaces.

sam: OK. Two security asks before full approve: 1) add explicit migration doc (steps + rollback) in the PR description, 2) add audit logging hook for KMS operations (or a ticket to add asap) — we need KMS usage logged to the tenant audit stream. If you can add a config flag require_audit_log default true for enterprise/private, that helps.

maya: Will add migration doc and flip require_audit_log default. I'll also open a follow-up ticket for tenant-audit integration for KMS calls and link it in the PR.
